summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update34.json → valid=true). Complemented the snapshot-install finding with the publisher side, recorded as a protective-mechanism negative with its residual wart stated. Creating a snapshot writes into a temporary directory, flushes and syncs the state file, writes and syncs the metadata inside that same temporary directory, renames the directory into its final name, syncs the parent directory, and only then reaps (file_snapshot.go:397-445) — so a crash leaves either a temporary directory that every listing skips or a complete published snapshot, never a listed-but-incomplete one; cancellation removes the temporary directory rather than publishing (450-467); listings skip temporary directories and directories with unreadable or unsupported metadata and return the remainder in reverse term-then-index order, i.e. newest first (245-296), which retention then uses to keep the first entries and delete the rest (365-380); and the constructor refuses a retention below one (88-96), which is what makes the catastrophic hypothesis unreachable — a store configured to publish a snapshot and then immediately delete it would leave a compacted log with no snapshot and an unstartable node, and that configuration simply cannot be created. Two honest caveats recorded: the ordering key is term then index, which equals newest-first only because a single node's term and index grow together (a directory manipulated out of band could interleave differently), and reaping runs inside the close path, so a reaping failure is reported as a failure of the snapshot that was in fact already published, leaving the raft layer's in-memory snapshot index and log compaction un-advanced — an error-attribution wart noted rather than filed as a finding. Counterevidence preserved: the atomicity argument rests on the rename being the sole naming step and on the metadata preceding it (no crash was injected), a crash between rename and parent sync is bounded by that sync (skipped only on Windows, as documented), and a crashed creation leaves a temporary directory that costs disk until an operator removes it.
